lessons.title: Direct and Indirect Speech
lessons.concept: Direct speech reports the exact words spoken, usually inside quotation marks. Indirect (reported) speech conveys the meaning of what was said without quoting the exact words, often requiring changes in pronouns, tense, and time/place expressions.
lessons.formula: Direct: He said, "I am busy." Indirect: He said that he was busy.
lessons.worked_example: Direct: Rina said, "I like coffee." Indirect: Rina said that she liked coffee.
mistakes: Keeping quotation marks in indirect speech
Not changing pronouns to match the reporting context
Forgetting to adjust tense when reporting verb is in past
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Tense and Pronoun Changes
lessons.concept: When the reporting verb is in the past (e.g., said), the tense in the reported clause often shifts back (present -> past, present perfect -> past perfect, etc.) in indirect speech. Pronouns and possessives also change based on speaker/listener perspective.
lessons.formula: Common backshift: am/is -> was, are -> were, have/has -> had, will -> would, can -> could. Pronouns change by context (I -> he/she, my -> his/her).
lessons.worked_example: Direct: He said, "I have finished my work." Indirect: He said that he had finished his work.
mistakes: Applying backshift when it is not required (e.g., universal truths in some contexts)
Changing pronouns mechanically without considering meaning
Mixing tense backshift inconsistently within one sentence
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Reporting Questions and Commands
lessons.concept: Reported questions use reporting verbs like asked/inquired and usually do not keep question word order or question marks. Yes/no questions use if/whether; wh-questions keep the wh-word. Commands/requests use told/asked/ordered + to-infinitive (or not to).
lessons.formula: Yes/no: asked if/whether + statement order. Wh-: asked + wh-word + statement order. Command: told/asked + object + to/not to + verb.
lessons.worked_example: Direct: She asked, "Where do you live?" Indirect: She asked where I lived. Direct: He said, "Close the door." Indirect: He told me to close the door.
mistakes: Keeping question mark or interrogative word order in reported questions
Using 'that' instead of if/whether for yes/no questions
Using 'said to' incorrectly for commands instead of 'told/asked/ordered'
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I am tired."

options.A: He said that he is tired.
options.B: He said that he was tired.
options.C: He said that I was tired.
options.D: He told that he was tired.

practice.explanation: With past reporting verb 'said', present 'am' backshifts to 'was' and pronoun 'I' changes to 'he': He said that he was tired.

options.B: She said that she had finished her homework.
options.C: She said that I had finished my homework.
options.D: She told that she had finished her homework.

practice.explanation: Present perfect 'have finished' backshifts to past perfect 'had finished', and pronouns/possessives change appropriately.

options.A: He asked that I was coming.
options.B: He asked if I was coming.
options.D: He said if I am coming.

practice.explanation: Yes/no questions in indirect speech use 'if/whether' and statement word order: He asked if I was coming.

practice.question: Change to indirect speech: The teacher said, "Open your books."

options.A: The teacher said to open your books.
options.B: The teacher told us open our books.
options.C: The teacher told us to open our books.
options.D: The teacher asked that we open your books.

practice.explanation: Commands are reported with 'told/asked/ordered + object + to-infinitive'. Pronoun 'your' changes to 'our' in this context.

practice.question: Change to indirect: He said, 'I am tired.'

options.A: He said that he was tired.
options.B: He said that he is tired.
options.C: He says that he was tired.
options.D: He told that I am tired.

practice.explanation: Reporting past speech backshifts present 'am' to past 'was', and first-person 'I' changes to third-person 'he'. 'That' is optional; 'told' needs an object.

practice.question: In indirect speech, the reporting verb is usually placed:

options.B: Before the reported clause, with a comma removed and 'that' optionally added

practice.explanation: Structure becomes: reporter + said (that) + clause. Quotation marks disappear and the comma of direct speech is removed.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: Meena said, "I will go to Delhi tomorrow."

options.A: Meena said that she will go to Delhi tomorrow.
options.B: Meena said that she would go to Delhi the next day.
options.C: Meena said that I would go to Delhi the next day.
options.D: Meena told that she would go to Delhi tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Backshift 'will' -> 'would', pronoun 'I' -> 'she', and time expression 'tomorrow' -> 'the next day' in reported speech.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: He asked, "Where is the station?"

options.A: He asked where the station was.
options.B: He asked where was the station.
options.C: He asked that where the station is.
options.D: He said where the station was.

questions.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but use statement word order in indirect speech: 'where the station was'.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: She said, "I can solve this problem."

options.A: She said that she can solve that problem.
options.B: She said that she could solve that problem.
options.C: She said that I could solve this problem.
options.D: She told that she could solve this problem.

questions.explanation: Modal 'can' backshifts to 'could', 'this' often becomes 'that', and pronoun 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: The manager said to the team, "Please submit the report today."

options.A: The manager requested the team to submit the report that day.
options.B: The manager said the team to submit the report today.
options.C: The manager requested that the team submits the report today.
options.D: The manager told to the team to submit the report that day.

questions.explanation: A polite request is reported with 'requested/asked + object + to-infinitive'. 'Today' changes to 'that day' in indirect speech.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I bought this book yesterday."

options.A: He said that he bought that book yesterday.
options.B: He said that he had bought that book the previous day.
options.C: He said that he has bought this book the previous day.
options.D: He said that I had bought that book the previous day.

questions.explanation: Simple past often backshifts to past perfect in reported speech: 'bought' -> 'had bought'; 'this' -> 'that'; 'yesterday' -> 'the previous day'.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Change to indirect: The teacher said to the students, 'You must submit the assignment.'

options.A: The teacher told the students that you must submit the assignment.
options.B: The teacher told the students that they must/had to submit the assignment.
options.C: The teacher said students to must submit the assignment.
options.D: The teacher said to students to submitted the assignment.

questions.explanation: 'Said to' with an addressee becomes 'told'; second-person 'you' becomes 'they' (the students); the modal can stay 'must' or shift to 'had to'. Option B is the only complete, grammatical conversion.

questions.question: The pronoun change from 'I' to 'he' in indirect speech is driven by:

options.B: Change of person/deixis relative to the reporter
options.D: Whether the sentence has a question mark

questions.explanation: Person shifts relative to the new speaker: first person becomes third when the reporter differs from the original speaker; second person maps to the listener's identity.

questions.question: Convert: She said to him, 'What are you doing?' (indirect)

options.A: She asked him what he was doing.
options.B: She asked him what are you doing.
options.C: She told him what he is doing.
options.D: She said him what was he doing.

questions.explanation: Wh-questions become indirect with statement word order (no inversion): asked + object + what + subject + verb. 'Are' backshifts to 'was'; 'you' becomes 'he'.
